question:
For Yamal, Gydan and Taimyr oil and gas, which changes to shipping, trans-shipment, product form or field sequencing would raise delivered tonnes per year from capacity already built or sanctioned, and cut full cost per tonne delivered to a buyer that can legally pay? The comparison is Yamal LNG, Arctic LNG 2 and Vostok Oil/Vankor. The answer must use only Russian-built hulls, liquefaction trains and equipment (Zvezda, Arctic Cascade/Mix, Kazanskompressormash, Kriogenmash, Power Machines) and must not depend on getting around sanctions.
Cases: Arctic LNG 2 trains 1–3 at Utrenneye; Yamal LNG; Murmansk/Ob LNG concepts; Vostok Oil (Payakha, Bukhta Sever terminal, 30 Mt/y target in H2 2027); Taimyr coking coal from Syradasayskoye via Dikson, which shares the Kara Sea route, icebreakers and season.
A good answer: (a) full cost per tonne delivered, including idle sunk capex, trans-shipment and buyer discount (Arctic LNG 2 cargoes sell 30–40% below market); (b) years to first delivered cargo or added cargo; (c) utilisation of built capacity, Kara Sea and Ob Gulf operating days per year for each hull class, and life of pads and pipelines on ice-rich Yamal ground.
The binding constraint to attack: Ice-class hulls (2 Arc7 LNG carriers available to Russia, 21 contracted), winter access to the Ob Gulf, which only Arc7 ships can reach, and legal access to buyers (EU LNG ban and EU tanker and icebreaker service bans from 2027; Rosneft on the US SDN list since Oct 2025).
This is part 2 of 3 of a larger question (context, not instructions): Russia wants to develop and extract minerals and energy in its permafrost regions at the lowest full cost, in the shortest time from investment decision to first production, and with the highest effectiveness. Effectiveness means resource recovery, working time across the year, and how long infrastructure lasts on thawing ground. All three are measured per unit of product delivered to the buyer. T
notes:
The asker wants a professional, deeply sourced answer: hundreds of sources, numbers with units and years. Use official
Russian statistics and registers (Rosstat, Rosnedra, the Ministry of Natural Resources and its state reports on
mineral resources), company annual reports and presentations (Nornickel, Alrosa, Polyus, Rosneft, Novatek,
Gazprom Neft, Udokan Copper, Kaz Minerals for Baimskaya, Elga Coal), Russian-language technical literature (for
example the Melnikov Permafrost Institute of SB RAS and mining journals) as well as international sources. Proposals
must not depend on circumventing sanctions.
Assumptions in the question that may be wrong:

- The three measures can be traded off against each other, and one ordering of deposits is best.
- Thaw is the main cause of infrastructure failure, though engineering faults may be as important.
- All listed resources are in continuous permafrost, though some sit in discontinuous or no permafrost.
- The NSR is the main way to move product, but rail, river, or processing near the site may beat it.
- More output is the goal, though some listed projects may not be worth building at all.
Where deciding data may exist:

- Rosatom/NSR administration traffic statistics and ice-class fleet lists.
- Russian Ministry of Natural Resources (Rosnedra) reserves balance, the GKZ.
- Company reports from Nornickel, Polyus, Kinross-era Kupol, Novatek, Rosneft, Alrosa and Mechel/Elga.
- Permafrost temperature records: GTN-P and the Roshydromet/Earth Cryosphere Institute (Moscow) monitoring networks.
- Rostekhnadzor accident reports.
- Published capex and opex of the foreign benchmark mines (technical reports under Canadian NI 43-101 rules).
- Global Energy Monitor or IEA-style cost data for LNG.
What the parts share or compete for: - **Icebreakers:** the four project 22220 icebreakers in service, with Chukotka due in 2027, serve Part 2 (Ob Gulf, Kara Sea), Part 3 (year-round Dudinka) and Part 1 (Pevek in the eastern sector).
reframes: Given the Arc7 LNG carriers, Arc7 tankers and nuclear icebreaker hours actually available each year to 2028, which allocation across Arctic LNG 2, Yamal LNG, Vostok Oil and Dikson coal maximises legally sold tonnes per year and minimises marginal cost per added delivered tonne? The decision variables are shuttle length (Ob Gulf or Bukhta Sever to the trans-shipment point) and season split.

Which product form and route reaches buyers who can pay without sanctions exposure after 1 Jan 2027, for each stream? Examples are Yamal LNG volume displaced from the EU, Arctic LNG 2 cargoes, Rosneft crude, and coal. What discount does each pay?
